title: Specified completion comparison isomorphism on complete inputs
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embedding $\iota:E\to F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $X$. Let $R_E,R_F$ be their completed integral coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use the derived categories of sheaves of modules over them [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $C_\iota K=K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_F$ for ordinary derived scalar extension and $U_\iota K$ for the strict quotient-tower scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For a derived-complete $K\in D(R_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete], define the comparison isomorphism $b_{\iota,K}:C_\iota K\xrightarrow{\sim}U_\iota K$ to be the specified natural completion comparison $\chi_{\iota,K}$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], equipped with the invertibility proved there. Thus its forward arrow is exactly that comparison and its inverse is the inverse of that same arrow, not a new completion map. Coefficient and scheme universes are independent for this construction. For an intrinsic integral constructible object $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], use the canonical proof that its underlying object satisfies this derived-completeness predicate, obtained by identifying the augmented reduction triangles; in this intrinsic presentation the coefficient field and scheme have the same universe. This supplies $b_{\iota,K}$ on integral constructible inputs without an additional completeness hypothesis.
